text:
Alice W: quick heads-up — Go SDK generator streams don't seem to respect ctx cancel reliably. started a small repro in the sample app and hit a goroutine leak after canceling.
Ben K: can you paste the snippet? I thought Stream.Recv() used ctx internally.
Alice W: here's the minimal flow from the sample app:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator("gpt-4r").Stream(ctx, prompt)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  tok, err := stream.Recv()
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { log.Printf("recv err: %v", err); break }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
```
Alice W: after cancel() the loop never returns, the goroutine stuck in Recv() and memory climbs.
Carlos M: hm. Are you on the latest SDK? We changed the transport retry behavior recently. Might be related if the transport retries masks context cancellation.
Alice W: running v0.9.2 (the sample app pinned to it). Also noticed when auth token refresh happens mid-stream, the SDK issues an internal retry which seems to replay partially-streamed chunks — duplicates show up in the client output.
Ben K: that sounds like two separate problems: 1) Recv not returning on ctx.Done(), 2) retries causing duplicated chunks. Agree?
Alice W: yep. Both hit real apps — cancellations for users hitting back button, and duplicate tokens for real-time viewers. UX is bad.
Ben K: for (1) I think our HTTP stream read is blocking on the body reader and we're only checking ctx on request creation. We need to make the read loop select on ctx.Done() and a chan of parsed tokens.
Ben K: for (2) IIRC the retry middleware currently retries on 5xx/429/401 and tunnels the response through the same stream object. For streaming we should NOT do a full request retry — at best we can signal a terminal error to the consumer and let the app decide to restart the stream.
Carlos M: agree. Streaming semantics should be "no automatic retry" by default. Maybe an opt-in flag like WithStreamNoRetry or a RetryPolicy that returns false for streaming.
Alice W: suggested API change (proposal):
```go
stream, err := client.Generator("x").Stream(ctx, prompt, api.WithNoRetry(), api.WithStreamHandler(handler))
```
Alice W: also propose Stream.Recv() returns context.Canceled if ctx canceled and ensures underlying goroutine exits.
Ben K: sounds good. Implementation note: the transport layer needs a cancelable io.Reader wrapper that unblocks Read when ctx canceled.
Ben K: also let's add a tiny sample app in /examples/go/stream-cancel that demonstrates proper ctx cancellation and minimal server-side behavior. That will reduce onboarding friction.
Carlos M: +1 on sample. Would help QA: include tests that assert no goroutine leak after cancel and no duplicate tokens when auth refresh occurs.
Alice W: QA found a small repro for the auth-dup bug: when token refresh happens mid-stream, we re-POST the same request and merge the second response into the original stream buffer.
Alice W: I can open an issue with logs and the repro harness.
Ben K: please do. Tag me and Carlos. I'll prototype the cancelable reader tomorrow.
Alice W: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/432 — added logs and sample harness. @Ben K @Carlos M
dev-bot: issue created by Alice W — "go generator stream cancel + retry semantics" (#432) :white_check_mark:
Carlos M: thanks. short-term fix idea: disable retries for requests with a Stream flag in transport, and add a ConcurrencySafePush for chunks so duplicates can be de-duplicated if they happen.
Alice W: de-duping is okay as bandaid, but prefer not to rely on it. main thing: make cancel immediate and document the new behavior in the Go quickstart. onboarding notes: call out WithNoRetry for long-lived streams and show cancel patterns.
Ben K: I'll add a PR that: 1) adds cancelable reader, 2) exposes WithNoRetry option for streams, 3) adds example app and a small test. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Alice W: amazing — thanks. linking sample in the SDK README will help reduce confusion for folks hitting this in prod. :shipit:
Ben K: noted. I'll also add a short note in CHANGELOG about streaming semantics change and the recommended pattern for backpressure/cancel.
Alice W: can we also update the JS/Python SDK docs so parity is obvious? Our support team keeps getting questions about "why JS cancels but Go doesn't".
Carlos M: yes — once change lands I'll coordinate docs sync with docs team.
dev-bot: linked issue #432 to milestone "sdk-go-0.9.3" and added label "streaming" :gear:
Alice W: thanks all, I'll follow up on the issue with the repro results and sample app path.
